newsitem.title: USA: Dow off, overall market mixed at midday.
newsitem.headline: Dow off, overall market mixed at midday.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were mixed at midday Thursday as the Dow industrials fell prey to profit taking after a rally which them over 7,000 for the first time in nearly seven weeks.
Not only is the Dow coming off a strong move, one that saw it rally about 270 points in three days, but investors are wary ahead of the April employment report due tomorrow.
The Dow was down 48 at 6961 while advances led declines by 14 to 10 on volume of about 244 million shares. NYSE curbs have been in place since 1117 EDT/1517 GMT.
U.S. Treasuries, responding to a favorable April NAPM, were firm, with the long bond up 13/32 to yield 6.93 percent.
The high techs extended their rally, taking the Nasdaq Composite Index up 10 points, or 0.76 percent, to 1270.

"The Dow's pullback can be accounted for," said Anthony O'Bryan, technical analyst at A.G. Edwards & Sons. "The average deserves a rest because blue chips have been so strong lately and were vulnerable to some very normal profit-taking.
"Also, the employment report is critical. It ranks with the employment cost index as the indicator that (Federal Reserve chairman Alan) Greenspan watches."
O'Bryan said the market was fickle and people were taking some of their big profits off the table lest tomorrow's report changes the mood yet again.
"Everyone's mind-set changes quickly. Everyone was bearish a week ago. Now they are bullish. You get a terrible number tomorrow and everyone might start selling again," he said.

Roy Blumber, chief investment strategist at Josephthal Lyon & Ross, said that the market was seeing ordinary profit-taking today. He added that even a strong employment number tomorrow may not cause more than a 30-point decline in the Dow industrials.
He attributes the strength in the market to lingering good will caused by last Monday's lower than forecast first quarter employment cost index.

"The ECI data neutralized most of the other numbers this week. Yesterday's GDP numbers were ignored by the market," he said. "I think that if we get a terrible number in the jobs report there will be minimal downside. We may go down 30 points or so on the Dow, but it won't be a debacle du jour."
He said that the market's performance today was positive.
"Breadth on the NYSE is still positive and even secondaries are trying to get into the act," he said.
A continued rally in technology stocks on Thursday extended to small capitalization stocks, which have been overlooked during the recent market recovery.

Micron Technology Inc, the most actively traded NYSE issue, was up two at 37-1/4. Cisco Systems Inc, the msot actively traded Nasdaq issue, was up 1-3/8 at 53-1/8, Adobe Systems was up 2-7/16 at 41-9/16, 3Com Corp was up 2-1/8 at 31-1/8.
Shares of CIGNA Corp rose 4-1/4 to 154-5/8 after the company posted better-than-expected first quarter profits.
